unresolved_added: The official prompt is unavailable in the source package; the paper's internal task reconstruction is not the official wording.
Product review counts are treated as cumulative sales, with no traffic, conversion, returns, price or exposure data.
The assumptions exclude spam, bias and missing records without an independent audit.
Wrong-category sparse products are removed wholesale; the threshold and omitted products need a sensitivity ledger.
The hair-spray and fridge examples establish data cleaning need but not the full scope of category contamination.
Same-day purchase/review timing is unrealistic for shipping, use and confirmation delays.
One review per customer/product is assumed without user-level verification.
Rating 1/5 and 2/4 symmetry removes ordinal direction before the separate polarity matrix restores sign.
The rating impact parameter λ is initially set to one without calibration.
Vine status is assigned a factor of two from a trust narrative, not a measured reliability comparison.
Verified buyers receive one and unverified buyers 0.1, but the values are not probabilities or sensitivity-calibrated weights.
AFINN's 2,477-word lexicon and local filtering omit synonyms, domain terms, context, negation and sarcasm.
Several word grades are manually changed with no change list, annotator agreement or reproducible rule.
A review with no matched sentiment word is assigned a correction value of one, which conflates absence of evidence with neutral baseline.
The maximum word grade discards within-review sentiment mixture and word frequency.
The polarity matrix turns each review into one sign despite mixed positive and negative language.
Helpfulness votes are affected by exposure, position and popularity and are not pure trust.
The helpfulness factor has a discontinuity in its special zero-vote branch and its exact OCR/implementation needs replay.
Logarithmic review length still rewards verbosity and does not measure readability or factual correctness.
The negation check counts adjective combinations but does not test scope, punctuation or multiword constructions.
The 1.15% ignore decision has no uncertainty interval or downstream sensitivity analysis.
The exponential time weight `a=1.1` is chosen without estimation or cross-validation.
The weight indexing and normalization direction need an independent formula/code check.
Reputation is a dot product of a constructed score and weights, not a validated latent reputation measure.
Sales are derived from review counts, so reputation-versus-sales correlation can be circular.
The evaluation selects three best sellers and one poor seller per product before broader claims.
Kendall tau measures rank association, not equality of levels, predictive accuracy or causal effect.
“Strong correlation proves correctness” overstates a proxy comparison.
GPR is chosen for small data and intervals, but kernel, noise, hyperparameters and priors are not frozen.
The short-horizon held-out plot is not a complete calibration report.
Long-horizon points outside the interval expose forecast error, but the proposed all-record repair is not validated.
Using a smoother reputation proxy may hide abrupt sales changes.
The logistic mapping bounds predictions but does not repair underlying extrapolation.
The constant .5 successfulness threshold is arbitrary.
The age-dependent threshold is fitted by design intuition rather than held-out calibration.
Reclassified products are looked up in the same source data, not independently validated.
k-event grouping assumes the next review is exposed to the preceding same-rating streak.
Event windows can overlap or be dependent, but independence is not addressed.
Top-5 models are selected by the same review-count sales proxy used in weighting.
High-rating events are common in best sellers while low-rating events are sparse, creating directional evidence imbalance.
Expanding to 95% of models improves coverage but does not create missing low-rating events.
The supported high-rating result is associative and should not be called incitement without identification.
The paper correctly refuses to determine low-rating incitement, but the letter should preserve that refusal.
Word appearance is counted once per review, which changes the estimand from token frequency to document presence.
Top-5 word tables are small samples and need the later frequent-word check.
The frequent-word threshold of 50 is arbitrary and multiple testing is not corrected.
Word star-rates are conditional associations, not sentiment calibration or product-quality causation.
Positive/negative descriptors can be used ironically or in mixed contexts.
Competition intensity is a sales-weighted average of constructed reputation, not a market-share or loyalty estimate.
The branch “enough effort” versus “limited effort” lacks budget, cost, margin and conversion data.
Noun filtering can discard verbs/adjectives that contain design requirements.
Top mention counts do not estimate willingness to pay or engineering importance.
Product feature suggestions require safety, regulatory and usability review, especially for pacifiers and microwaves.
Sensitivity changes one parameter at a time and does not test interactions or joint uncertainty.
The claim of general robustness conflicts with visible late-horizon sensitivity to `a`.
Strengths are self-reported and partly repeat the model's own proxy outcomes.
The weaknesses admit arbitrariness but do not specify which coefficients or rules should be replaced first.
The word-set limitation can systematically omit domain-specific and non-adjective evidence.
Code appendices lack a frozen environment, input bundle, seed, complete outputs and independent rerun report.
OCR damages symbols, signs, subscripts and Chinese/Unicode fragments; original raster remains authoritative.
References and cited literature support context, not validation of this implementation.
Appendix tables and code are retained as evidence but excluded from author positive-language counts.
The company letter states score/reputation reliability more strongly than the long-horizon evidence allows.
The letter turns review-count proxies into profit/sales language without causal identification.
Product-specific actions are not linked to cost, staffing, safety, legal, equity or reversal criteria.
The source's “customers' voices” framing is useful prose but does not solve selective review participation.
The title and manager memo are retained for source role, not counted as analytical body moves.
The final conclusion appropriately preserves high-rating evidence and low-rating uncertainty; this asymmetry must survive reuse.
Any future master-skill rule must keep “This is not appropriate”, explicit overfit failure and “cannot determine” as evidence-boundary moves.
Exact product names, IDs, thresholds, word percentages and letter claims must not be copied as defaults into another paper.
